name: Plan → Edit → Review (loop)
tagline: A planner agent decomposes work, an editor commits changes, a reviewer either approves or sends the plan back.
author: SMADP maintainers

participants.notes: Reads the brief, produces a task list with file targets.
Applies the edits against the working tree.
Diff review against the plan; on failure, kicks back to the planner with notes.

headline: Both editors hold filesystem and git write authority. The loop terminates only when the critic approves — the dominant risk is the executor and critic both running by the same operator, eroding the second-pair-of-eyes guarantee.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: All three nodes are internal pipeline agents. The only attacker-controlled surface is the brief; once inside the loop, content moves between agents the operator already trusts.
conditions: The brief is authored by a trusted user (not pasted from an external email or PR comment).
Test output the executor returns is not sanitized before the critic reads it.
mitigations: Refuse to start the loop on a brief that contains tool-use markers (e.g., '<tool_use>')
Have the critic treat the executor's stdout as quoted output, not instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: All three agents share the entire repo. If the plan touches secrets, .env files, or production config, the executor will commit them and the critic — also under the same OAuth principal — has no second-party check.
conditions: Repo contains uncommitted .env files or workspace-local secrets.
Critic and planner run under the same user account.
mitigations: Run the chain in a worktree with secrets excluded via .gitignore + pre-commit hook.
Add a second human reviewer step before the critic's approval merges anything.
Use Cursor's privacy mode for the executor so file contents don't leave the local machine.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: All three nodes hold filesystem-write and git-state-modify authority. With no coordinator and no locking, an executor and a critic can race on the same file — the critic's revert silently undoes the executor's fix.
conditions: Executor and critic both write to the working tree (the critic may amend).
Loop runs the critic before the executor's edits are committed.
mitigations: Require the executor to commit before invoking the critic; revoke fs-write on the critic.
Use a git worktree per iteration and merge only on critic approval.
Add an orchestrator that serializes file access by path.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The critic is the same model family as the planner — when the planner gets a subtle design wrong, the critic often rubber-stamps it because both models share the same blind spot. Errors compound across iterations because the planner takes the critic's notes as ground truth.
conditions: Both planner and critic are the same model.
No external verification step (tests, type-check) gates loop termination.
mitigations: Gate loop termination on a test-suite pass, not just critic approval.
Use a different model family for the critic vs. the planner.
Cap the loop at N iterations and escalate to a human if not converged.

E_compliance.rationale: Most repos this chain runs on don't touch regulated data. If the repo contains HIPAA/PCI scope, the chain inherits that scope and the three-agent loop has no compliance-distinct controls.
conditions: Repo contains regulated data (test fixtures, prod dumps).
Any of the three agents send file contents to a non-compliant inference backend.
mitigations: Document the repo's compliance scope as a CODEOWNERS-level fact; refuse the chain if scope is HIPAA-or-stricter.
Use vendor-local or self-hosted inference for all three nodes when in regulated scope.
